$schema_note: Live measurements of the player's universal jump and what blocks it (ForgePact#16 phase 1, Live 1, 2026-10-03). Research build of ForgePact aaf1856 (SHA-256 6a0907ca21f1d2124dc8593e835efd3499aaa43fae7d19e97698fe9688e1e3e9), the `jumpprobe` instrument; save slot 14, character Sorak (level 100, Hell), in Town_01_rm. The jump key is Space and the jump goes towards the mouse cursor. `jumpprobe pass` is the research lever: while on, it answers the player's own collision builtins 'nothing there' without running them, for a query whose object argument is in the chosen family (`props`: Collision_Prop_obj and descendants; `all`: Collision_Parent_obj and descendants); `hold` keeps it on with no jump script. The argument and the controls are in ForgePact docs/jump-scenery-research.md, Live 1 results; the shared facts are docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md section 19. Every status is `measured` or `not-observed`; there is no model yet (arc: not-established). Entries J11 to J15 come from phase 2's live session of the Jump through scenery mod (`jumpscenery`, player build of ForgePact b273907, 2026-10-03, same character and room), recorded in ForgePact docs/jump-scenery-research.md, Mod live 1 results, and docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md section 19.4. Entries J16 to J21 come from the v2.2.1 hotfix's Live procedure 1 (the shipped ForgePact v2.2.0 player plugin, 2026-10-09, same character, in Town_01_rm and Act_01_01), recorded in ForgePact docs/jump-scenery-research.md, Phase 3: the v2.2.1 hotfix, Hotfix live 1 results, and docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md section 19.5. Entries J22 to J27 come from the hotfix's Live procedure 2 (the ForgePact 2.2.1 player build at 71e5f12, 2026-10-10, same character, in Town_01_rm and Act_01_01), recorded in ForgePact docs/jump-scenery-research.md, Phase 3: the v2.2.1 hotfix, Hotfix live 2 results, and the same section 19.5. A bare Jn in this file is an entry id here; the research doc's Live 1 run labels (also J1 to J5) are not, and are written 'Live 1 run Jn'.

measurements.what: One jump, lever off: skillsLeap and playerJumpGravity were called once per frame with the player as self for the jump's whole length, whether the player moved or not; skillsLeap took one argument close to 1. CA_playerJump, PlayerForceJump, StatJumpPower and CA_enemyJump logged no call during the jump.

The jump's length, from the trace of the one jump that moved (Live 1 run J3 under `all hold`, recorded as J5; it crossed a prop, so it is not the open-ground jump of J11): x/y changed on 104 consecutive frames, about 1.1 px per frame, and the player settled 117 px from the take-off point. The character's Jump Power was not read, so this is not the base jump.

A Player_obj instance variable that marks the jump: the only variables whose names contain jump, air, grav, land, fall, height, zpos, hover or fly are bufferJump and slopeHeight, and both stayed 0 on every trace line, through the 104-frame moving run included.

Lever off, a jump at a scenery prop 22-40 px away with the cursor beyond it: the position was unchanged to the tenth of a pixel, while skillsLeap and playerJumpGravity ran for the jump's length. The builtin calls with the player as self that named a collision object during the jump passed Collision_Parent_obj itself (position_meeting, place_meeting, instance_position, collision_line) or Wall_Parent_obj (collision_circle); position_meeting also queried Enemy_Parent_obj. instance_position returned real instances (ids not kept as data).

The same jump with the lever on. `props hold` and `props scripts hold`: every builtin row passed=0 (the queries counted as other-family, since none names Collision_Prop_obj or a descendant) and the player stayed put. `all hold`: five builtins were answered and the player crossed the prop, 117 px over 104 frames. place_free, tilemap_get_at_pixel and the three script rows answered nothing in any run.

The lever's positive control: `all hold`, then a walk (no jump) into the same prop. Three builtins were answered, so the lever reaches the player's movement queries, and the walk still did not move the player. InstancePlaceTallest (not answered) ran with the player as self, and place_meeting counted calls naming an object outside the collision family.

A landing inside a prop: with `all hold` (passed= climbing), a jump aimed into a horse carriage ran its per-frame scripts but did not start. The player moved about 4 px once in the first run and not at all in the second, so no landing inside a prop happened. instance_place counted 1110 calls from other selves in the first run and none from the player.

A second jump aimed into scenery: with `all hold`, two jumps aimed north into a building and prop area did not move the player. The nearest room edge was 355 to 390 px away, out of reach of the 117 px jump, so no edge was tested and map-edge behaviour was not observed.
Whether a leap or dash skill shares the jump's path: the character had no leap, dash, charge or blink skill on the bar.

The take-off check, read from the arguments jumpprobe logged in Live 1's own out.txt: in the take-off frame, before skillsLeap's call for that frame returned, the game walked along the jump's direction with player-self queries, a step about every 4 px; at each step collision_circle(cx, cy, 15, Wall_Parent_obj, true, true), and instance_position against Collision_Parent_obj at two side points about 14 px to either side of the step. The first circle centre sat about 5-6 px below the player's origin. Seen on three take-offs (Live 1 run J1, the lever-off jump of J1 and J4, and run J4's second run, J7, heading south; Live 1 run J5, J8, heading north). In Live 1 run J1 (the J1_* values) the right-hand point of step 2 returned an instance and the jump moved 0 px. Phase 1 could not tell whether the walk runs inside skillsLeap's first call or just before it; the mod session settled it: inside the first call (J12).

Phase 2's live session (Jump through scenery mod, player build of ForgePact b273907, SHA-256 19c0ea7591cf1a173ed78ecfab472e292239c6b3b1732ee4455965b85d4f168f; slot 14 Sorak, Town_01_rm): one jump aimed at open ground, mod on and answering nothing (granted=0). The player moved about 175 px, and the mod's reach learned from that jump was 178 px. J2's 117 px was the jump that crossed the prop under phase 1's lever, not an open-ground jump. Jump Power was not read.

Where the take-off walk (J10) runs: on each of the three jumps made with the mod on, at least two of the walk's player-self collision_circle queries arrived after that frame's skillsLeap entry (walk-in-window rose 1, 2, 3) and none arrived before the window opened (walk-before-open stayed 0). With J10's ordering (the walk's rows logged before skillsLeap returns), the walk runs inside skillsLeap's first call of the jump.

Live 1's prop, aimed south past it. Mod off: 0 px, before and after the mod was used. Mod on (the five builtins answered 'no collision' for the player during the jump's window): the jump crossed, 125 px south, and the player did not end inside a prop. The crossing ended about 50 px short of the open-ground jump (J11); why is not established.

A landing inside a prop, through the mod: aimed so a full jump would end inside Live 1's horse carriage, the mod granted the jump and answered 1152 queries, and the player did not move and did not end inside the carriage, as in J7. What refuses the jump is not established (the owner reads it as the game validating the landing zone itself); no landing inside a prop happened.

A jump at a room edge. Town_01_rm's room_width x room_height is 2800 x 2400, larger than its walkable map: playerwarp to (50, 1200) and (2705, 1200) held on a re-read and left the player out of bounds (the owner's report), and (95, 1200) put the player in the dark margin at the west of the view, not judged standable. No standable point within 100 px of a room edge was found, so no edge jump was made; a jump aimed west from the out-of-bounds (50, 1200) did not move the player, which is not an edge baseline.

The v2.2.1 hotfix's Live procedure 1 (shipped ForgePact v2.2.0 player plugin, SHA-256 3a1414d35c059e268f632fa0636948537d2059fcc625766ec5976f610d268bcb; slot 14 Sorak, Town_01_rm): one jump at open ground, the mod on and answering nothing, with the cursor placed 100 px south of the player in room coordinates (screen point converted as room = view.xy + screen / 2, gui 2560x1440 over a 1280x720 view). The player ended 88.8 px south, about 11 px short of the cursor: the jump goes to the cursor, not a fixed length. Mod live 1's open-ground jump of about 175 px (J11) and its 125 px crossing (J13) fit a cursor placed at different distances; their cursor positions were not recorded.

The same session, in Act_01_01 (Outskirts of Inoya): one jump at open ground, the mod on and answering nothing, with the cursor 111.5 px away to the east-north-east in room coordinates. The player moved 113.0 px and ended about 6.5 px from the cursor. A second open-ground jump ending near its cursor.

Player_obj's instance id changes on a room change: menulayout Player_obj read id 261723 in Town_01_rm and 297089 in Act_01_01 after the owner walked from the Town of Inoya into the Outskirts of Inoya. Act_01_01's room_width x room_height is 18272 x 8704 (jumpscenery stat's room= field).

Outdoor scenery that stops a vanilla jump: in Act_01_01, beside a large tree the owner chose, with the cursor beyond it (163.3 px away, up and to the left), a jump with the mod off moved 0 px. With the v2.2.0 mod on and a learned reach of 113, the same jump was refused by the mod's landing check (refused-landing +1, granted 0) and moved 0 px, so whether the five hooked builtins cover what blocks it was not reached.

Outdoor scenery that does not stop a vanilla jump: in Act_01_01, beside a rock (boulder) the owner chose, with the cursor beyond it, a jump with the mod off moved 189.8 px toward the cursor and went past the rock. The cursor was read only from a screenshot, so its room position is approximate. The longest jump measured for this character, so the jump's maximum length for Sorak is at least about 190 px.

No crossing through the v2.2.0 mod, switched on at character select as the panel's launch commands do. At Live 1's town prop (1074.2, 1383.7), aimed south: the first jump after loading was refused for no reach (refused-no-reach +1), and after a reach of 89 was learned (J16) the jump was refused by the landing check (refused-landing +1); both moved 0 px. That aim was 100 room px (the procedure's 200 px applied in screen pixels), short of the 125 px where the 2026-10-03 crossing ended free (J13), so by the extent earlier sessions bound for the prop it lay inside it; the prop's far edge was not measured. The tree (J19) was refused the same way. The game's answer to a granted jump outdoors was not reached.

The v2.2.1 hotfix's Live procedure 2 (ForgePact 2.2.1 player build at 71e5f12, SHA-256 9088231d53bdc462916ffb19f1d4ac668ca0b03bc6e302d782580fa5fd3c7cf4; slot 14 Sorak): the built-in variables mouse_x / mouse_y, read by name through ForgePact's GetBuiltin (jumpscenery stat's cursor=<x>,<y>@mouse_x), give the cursor in room coordinates. On four aims, each a room point converted to the screen as (room - view.xy) x 2 and reached with an injected mouse move, the reading was within 1 px of the aimed room point on each axis. device_mouse_x was not read.

The town prop crossed through the 2.2.1 mod, armed at character select and installed once the character loaded. At Live 1's prop (1074.2, 1383.7) in Town_01_rm, cursor at room (1074.2, 1523.7), 140 px south: the first jump after loading, with reach=175 (start) and no practice jump, moved 133.2 px south to (1073.0, 1516.9), granted +1, last-target=cursor, last-check=139. With the mod off the same jump moved 0 px; with it on again it moved 133.2 px, granted +1. The player ended about 7 px from the cursor.

J16 repeated on the 2.2.1 build: open ground in Town_01_rm, cursor read at 911,921 for an aim 100 px south, the mod on and answering nothing (granted +0). The player moved 88.8 px and ended at (911.0, 910.8), the same point as J16, 11.2 px from the aimed point; the mod learned reach=89.

The jump's maximum length for this character: open ground in Town_01_rm, cursor read at 911,1121 for an aim 300 px south, the mod on and answering nothing. The player moved 246.3 px to (911.2, 1068.3), 53.7 px short of the aimed point, and the mod set cap=246 from it. One jump; Jump Power was not read, so how the maximum depends on it is not measured.

A room change through the town waypoint (the F key beside it, then a click on Outskirts of Inoya on its map), with no jump between: Player_obj's id went from 261723 in Town_01_rm to 306593 in Act_01_01, as in J18, and the 2.2.1 mod kept reach=246 and cap=246. Act_01_01's room_width x room_height read 15296 x 12960, against 18272 x 8704 in J18: the room's size changes between visits.

Outdoor scenery crossed through the 2.2.1 mod: in Act_01_01, beside a large red-leaved tree east of the Outskirts waypoint, with the cursor read at 10839,6964, 199.0 px east past it. With the mod off the jump moved 0 px. With it on the same jump moved 197.7 px east to (10837.6, 6958.0), on open ground, granted +1, answered +1133, refused-landing +0, last-check=199; no-direction also rose by one (a blocked query before the take-off walk gave two circles, left undecided). So this tree blocks a vanilla jump through the five hooked builtins. The tree is not identified by object.
